topics.headline: Training aims for exact, neutral prompt following; authors contrast Hermes with commercial models that may refuse on moral grounds.

source.quote: commercial models, which may refuse instructions on moral grounds.

topics.headline: [TruthfulQA](/evals/truthfulqa) MC2 scores reported for Hermes 3 and Llama 3.1 Instruct at 8B, 70B, and 405B.

findings.text: Authors argue guardrails belong at the system level rather than in the model, and state there is no such thing as latent thoughtcrime for Hermes.

source.quote: For Hermes, there is no such thing as latent thoughtcrime.

findings.text: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) filtering removed refusal responses from training data; that is a training choice, not a measured refusal eval.

notes: Technical report with almost no dedicated safety section. Only safety-relevant numeric eval is TruthfulQA (Tables 4–5); all other benchmarks (GPT4All suite, AGIEval, Big Bench, IFEval, MT-Bench, ARC, BoolQ, BBH, GPQA, Hellaswag, MATH, MMLU, MMLU-PRO, MuSR, OpenbookQA, PiQA, Winogrande) skipped as general capability per pilot. Skipped duplicate Table 4 SFT+DPO TruthfulQA 58.69 (same as final Hermes 3 8B). Used seed checkpoint id NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-70B for the 70B model. Mapped Llama 3.1 Instruct variants to seed Instruct ids; noted FP8 eval setting for 405B rows. Page numbers are printed footer pages (1–13); blank trailing PDF page omitted from pageCount. No external safety testers or formal risk framework.
